newsitem.title: FINLAND: OUTOKUMPU CEO SEES HIGHER ZINC PRICES - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: OUTOKUMPU CEO SEES HIGHER ZINC PRICES - RFTV.

text.p: Zinc prices will be higher in the next couple of years, Jyrki Juusela, CEO of Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu, said on Thursday.

"As we see the fundamentals in the future, the zinc prices are going to be better also for the next couple of years," Jyrki Juusela said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) after the group reported a clear improvement in January-April earnings.

Outokumpu's January-April profit before extraordinary items rose to 502 million markka from 305 million report and the group said it expected a clear improvement for the full year. In 1996, it posted a 229 million markka profit before extras.
Juusela said the four-month earnings were "very good", exceeding the group's 15 percent target return on capital employed. The profit was well above forecasts in a Reuters poll.

"We see the market fundamentals improving really very well and especially in the base metals (copper, nickel and zinc), and also we see improvement in our stainless steel market in the year," Juusela said.

Asked which of Outokumpu's sectors had most potential for growth, he said: "In the future (the most potential) will be in stainless steel because we are very strong already in stainless steel and we are increasing our capacity in stainless steel to serve our clients in the Europan markets."
He said zinc was the base metal with the most potential to generate growth for Outokumpu.
